name: time-split
title: Time Split
description: A total time on a raised panel, its split shown as coloured segments along the panel's curved bottom edge.

perf.budget: Segments trim one path on UI-thread springs on arrival and on change; the time re-renders only while it counts. Nothing animates at rest.

a11y.reducedMotion: Segments take their lengths and the time changes without gliding or counting.
a11y.screenReader: One label with the total and every item ("Studio Hours: 4 hours 36 minutes. Coding 2 hours 30 minutes, Reading 1 hour 1 minute.").

meta.guide:
## Usage

```tsx
import { TimeSplit } from '@/components/kinetik/time-split';

<TimeSplit
  title="Studio Hours"
  items={[
    { label: 'Sketching', minutes: 38 },
    { label: 'Coding', minutes: 112 },
    { label: 'Reviews', minutes: 44 },
    { label: 'Reading', minutes: 26 },
  ]}
/>;
```

## When to use

- A daily total and what it was spent on: screen time, focus time, a timesheet.
- Widgets, where the split matters as a shape more than as exact numbers.

## When not to use

- When people must compare exact amounts per item. The legend has no values, so use a bar chart.
- More than about six items: the segments get too short to tell apart.

## Notes

- The total is the sum of `minutes`; 90 reads as 01 : 30.
- Items are matched by `label`, so keep labels stable and each segment glides to its new length.
- The first and third colours tint the card's soft glow.

docs: Prefer `npx kinetik-ui add time-split`: it installs dependencies with expo install, so versions match your Expo SDK.
